item.title: Equational theories of min-plus semirings
item.description: arXiv:2611.03715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the equational theory and subvarieties of the variety $\mathcal V$ generated by $(\mathbb N_0,\min,+)$. We prove that a subvariety of $\mathcal V$ is proper if and only if it is locally finite, equivalently, if and only if it satisfies a power-stabilization identity. Every finite member generates a hereditarily finitely based variety with a finite subvariety lattice. In contrast, the periodic subvarieties defined by $x^m=x^{m+1}$ are nonfinitely based for $m\geq2$. We construct a strictly descending chain of nonfinitely based subvarieties and three varieties generated by explicit reduced products, each with a decidable equational theory. The smallest is a limit variety: it is nonfinitely based, and every proper subvariety has an absolute finite identity basis. The subvariety lattice of $\mathcal V$ has cardinality continuum. In fact, the interval between the first reduced-product variety and the subvariety defined by $x^2=x^3$ already has this cardinality, and all its members are nonfinitely based. We also give a hereditarily finitely based example with an infinite subvariety lattice. The constructions use finite convex models and recognition quotients.
item.dc:creator: Yilin Zhou, Zidong Gao

item.title: Friedman--Stanley cofinality without Borel completeness
item.description: arXiv:2611.04172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Friedman and Stanley asked whether an invariant Borel class of countable structures must be Borel complete whenever every countable level of their hierarchy reduces to it. We construct a counterexample in one fixed countable language. The structural counterexample and its principal supporting results have been formalized in Lean~4 and it is available on github.
item.dc:creator: Ruijun Wang

item.title: A Side Condition Principle With Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.04362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a combinatorial principle $\textsf{SC}(\kappa)$, for any regular cardinal $\kappa \ge \omega_2$, which asserts the existence of a family $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq [H(\kappa)]^\omega$ of elementary substructures of $H(\kappa)$ which is closed under finite intersections and satisfies that for stationarily many $N \in \mathcal{Y}$, if $M \in \mathcal{Y}$ and $M \cap \omega_1 < N \cap \omega_1$, then $M \cap N \cap \kappa \in N$. We explore the idea of defining forcings with side conditions consisting of finite subsets of such a family $\mathcal{Y}$. If $\textsf{SC}(\omega_2)$ holds, then there exists a thin stationary subset of $[\omega_2]^\omega$, and consequently $\textsf{SC}(\omega_2)$ is independent of ZFC. Assuming that $\mu$ is a Mahlo cardinal, the L\'{e}vy collapse $\mathrm{Col}(\omega,<\mu)$ forces that $\textsf{SC}(\kappa)$ holds for all regular cardinals $\kappa \ge \omega_2$. Local instances of $\textsf{SC}$ can be forced using matrices of models or derived as consequences of square principles. We apply the principle $\textsf{SC}$ to define two kinds of forcings: a streamlined version of a strongly proper collapse, and a forcing which is strongly proper on a stationary set and adds arbitrarily many Baumgartner clubs. Finally, we prove two consistency results using forcings derived from $\textsf{SC}$ related to Aronszajn trees, the guessing model principle, strong failures of club guessing, and the higher dominating number.
item.dc:creator: Hannes Jakob, John Krueger

item.title: Iterating logarithms and well-foundedness
item.description: arXiv:2611.04963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that there is no sequence $\{ X_n \}_{n\in\omega}$ such that for all $n$, there is an injection from $\mathcal{P}(X_{n+1})$ to $X_n$ under a restricted set of axioms that conforms to the "working mathematician's" intuition (excluding Choice, Replacement, and Foundation). We also show such a sequence cannot be defined using a formula either. More precisely, it is inconsistent with Zermelo set theory minus Infinity to have a formula $\Phi(\cdot,\cdot)$ such that for each $n\in\omega$ there are $X$ and $Y$ with $\Phi(n,X)$, $\Phi(n+1,Y)$, and $\mathcal{P}(Y)$ being injectable into $X$. We finally show that the theorem fails if we allow infinitely many definitions, one for each term of the sequence, by using Hamkins, Linetsky, and Reitz's pointwise definable extensions of countable models of ZFC.
item.dc:creator: Gervasio Figueroa, Joel Kuperman, Pedro S\'anchez Terraf

item.title: Large cardinals, small violations of choice
item.description: arXiv:2611.05140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relationship between large cardinals and Blass' Small Violation of Choice ($\mathsf{SVC}$), which states that the Axiom of Choice holds in a set-generic extension of the universe. Our main theorem is that in the presence of a supercompact cardinal, either the Axiom of Choice fails significantly, or else $\mathsf{SVC}$ holds in $L(\mathcal P(\mathrm{Ord}))$. We show that a supercompact is not strong enough to reflect $\mathsf{SVC}$, while an extendible cardinal is. If we assume Usuba's Lo\'s Property holds for the supercompact, then we can outright derive $\mathsf{SVC}$ in the universe.
item.dc:creator: Hope Duncan, Gabriel Goldberg, Asaf Karagila

item.title: The P-Ideal Dichotomy and the Failure of Two-Cardinal Square Principles
item.description: arXiv:2611.05198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the $\mathrm{P}$-ideal dichotomy implies the negation of the square principle $\square(\lambda, \omega)$ for every regular cardinal $\lambda\geq\omega_2$.
item.dc:creator: Victor Torres-Perez, Liuzhen Wu

item.title: Geometric classification of imaginaries in pseudofinite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.05248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In [Pil07], Pillay showed that every imaginary in a proper pair of algebraically closed fields is interalgebraic with an imaginary of a certain algebraic form. In this paper, we establish an analogue for lovely pairs of pseudofinite fields. After naming countably many constants, we prove that every imaginary in lovely pairs of pseudofinite fields is interalgebraic with an imaginary of the same algebraic form as [Pil07] in the corresponding pairs of finite extensions of pseudofinite fields.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Zhu

item.title: Hereditarily Lindel\"of and hereditarily separable subspaces of function spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.04911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A space is ESLC if it contains neither an $S$-space nor an $L$-space, and NFS is the class of spaces containing no free sequences of length $\omega_1$. We prove that under $\mathrm{MA}(\omega_1)$, if all finite powers of $X$ belong to NFS, then $C_p(X)^\omega$ is ESLC; thus, for subspaces of $C_p(X)$, hereditary Lindel\"ofness, hereditary separability and countable spread coincide. This is derived from a dual form of a theorem of Todor\v{c}evi\'c. A Lindel\"of $\Sigma$-space belongs to NFS if and only if its compact subspaces have countable tightness. Hence $C_p(X)$ contains no $L$-spaces if $X$ is a Lindel\"of $\Sigma$-space of countable tightness and $\mathrm{MA}(\omega_1)$ holds, or if $X$ is any Lindel\"of $\Sigma$-space and PFA holds. Under $\mathrm{MA}(\omega_1)$, all iterated function spaces of Corson compact spaces are ESLC, and in ZFC the space $C_p(X,\{0,1\})$ is ESLC for every zero-dimensional Corson compact space $X$.
item.dc:creator: Evgenii Reznichenko

item.title: Extended Contact Algebras: Algebraic analysis and duality theory
item.description: arXiv:2511.21396v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The ternary extended contact relation studied in (Ivanova, 2020) is a more expressive counterpart of the standard, well-known binary contact relation. Boolean algebras expanded with this relation are called Extended Contact Algebras (ECAs). In this work, we take an algebraic perspective on ECAs, interpreting the ternary relation as a form of entailment. To this end, we introduce the class of Pseudo-Inference Algebras, i.e., Boolean algebras equipped with a monotone ternary operator, additive in its first two coordinates, and satisfying additional equations that capture the logical character of the extended contact. We show that the subclass of relational Pseudo-Inference Algebras corresponds precisely to ECAs and generates the variety of strict PSI-Algebras, which is a discriminator variety. Furthermore, building on the duality developed in (Celani, 2009), we introduce descriptive PSI-frames and establish three interrelated dualities that differ in their morphisms while sharing the same class of topological objects. The resulting framework provides a relational semantics for PSI-Algebras, connecting spatial and logical notions within a categorical and topological setting.
item.dc:creator: Rafa{\l} Gruszczy\'nski, Paula Mench\'on, William Zuluaga

item.title: Amenable C-sequences and ineffability in L
item.description: arXiv:2610.09086v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a relative consistency counterexample to the conjecture of Inamdar and Rinot that every regular uncountable cardinal carrying no amenable C-sequence is ineffable in the constructible universe L. The existence of a $\Pi^2_1$-indescribable cardinal is equiconsistent with the existence of a $\Pi^2_1$-indescribable cardinal carrying no amenable C-sequence and not ineffable in L. For every ground-model C-sequence on a weakly compact cardinal $\kappa$, generalized Hechler forcing adds a club D with $D\cap\beta\subseteq C_\beta$ at stationarily many inaccessible indices. We use this capture theorem in an iteration of length $\kappa^+$ after Johnstone's local lottery preparation.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Fernandes

item.title: Omitting Types for Infinitary Real-Valued Logic: A Topological Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2611.02247v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For countable vocabularies, we extend the omitting types theorem for countable fragments of infinitary logic to Keisler's general real-valued structures by proving that the space of Henkin types of each such fragment is \v{C}ech-complete. The structures interpret function symbols arbitrarily and predicate symbols by bounded real-valued functions, while each formula carries a bound of its own. This extends the setting of Eagle's theorem from metric structures with a prescribed master metric to general structures whose vocabulary prescribes the sorts and bounds of the symbols. Following Keisler and Miller's treatment of logic without equality, we build models from closed terms. Morley's Baire category method then gives every satisfiable theory on a countable fragment a model with countable sorts omitting any countable family of types whose closed-term instances have empty interior in the space of Henkin types satisfying the theory.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Aubone, Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Convex algebras on an interval with semicontinuous monotone operations
item.description: arXiv:2603.14955v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent work of Matteo Mio on compact quantitative equational theories (here compact means that all its consequences are derivable by means of finite proofs) convex algebras on the carrier set [0,1] whose operations are monotone and satisfy certain semicontinuity properties occurred. We fully classify those algebraic structures by giving an explicit construction of all possible convex operations on [0,1] possessing the mentioned properties. Our result thus describes exactly the range of theories to which Mio's theorem applies.
item.dc:creator: Ana Sokolova, Harald Woracek

item.title: Univalence without function extensionality
item.description: arXiv:2605.00812v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is a well-known theorem of homotopy type theory, originally due to Voevodsky, that function extensionality holds inside any univalent universe. We consider a weaker variant of the univalence axiom, asserting that the wild category formed by the universe is univalent, which we call categorical univalence. We show that categorical univalence does not imply function extensionality by an analysis of Von Glehn's polynomial model construction, which produces models of Martin-L\"of type theory that always refute function extensionality. We find in particular that when the base model has a univalent universe, its polynomial model has a universe that is categorically univalent but lacks function extensionality.
item.dc:creator: Evan Cavallo, Jonas H\"ofer

item.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
item.description: arXiv:2610.12434v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study whether global asymptotic stability (GAS) of the origin is decidable for homogeneous polynomial vector fields with rational coefficients. Our main technical contribution is showing that, for such vector fields of odd degree $d \geq 3$ in every sufficiently large dimension $n$, the problem of deciding GAS of the origin is many-one complete for the class of recursively enumerable sets (and hence undecidable). Using the tools we have built up, we also improve on some recent work by proving a similar result for Lyapunov stability instead of GAS. The proof of our main contribution splits naturally into two parts: - In the first part we give, for every fixed dimension $n$ and odd degree $2k+1$, a computable map which sends a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree $2k+1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ to a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree three on $\mathbb{R}^m$, where $m=\binom{n+k-1}{k}$, and preserves both GAS and Lyapunov stability. As a consequence, the problems of deciding whether the origin is GAS or Lyapunov stable for rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields of any degree, of any fixed odd degree $d \geq 3$, and of degree three are pairwise many-one equivalent. - In the second part we prove that there is a fixed dimension $n_*$ and a fixed odd degree $d_*$ such that the set of rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^{n_*}$ of degree $d_*$ whose origin is GAS is many-one complete. This is done by "transferring" many-one completeness between several different problems, starting from the solvability of a Diophantine equation and eventually arriving at our desired GAS decision problem.
item.dc:creator: Ivan O. Shevchenko, Jun Liu, Xinzhi Liu

item.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.02070v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.
item.dc:creator: Mladen Pavicic
